decision_rule: Fire if the maximum per-patch P(elephant) over the clip exceeds selected_threshold. Elephant calls are short events (~1 patch), so max-pooling is used instead of mean-pooling.
operating_point_rationale: Chosen for a conservation early-warning use case: maximize recall (never miss an elephant) at the cost of some false positives. On the 10 bundled demo samples this yields recall=1.00 (5/5 elephants detected) and 3 false positives that are a genuine model-discrimination limitation (see known_limitations).

live_debounce.note: Live detector requires M of the last K analysis windows to fire before confirming, suppressing momentary false positives.

known_limitations: The shipped elephant_xgb.json is the per-patch model. Some non-elephant clips (e.g. Non_9_10928, Non_16_11656) contain patches that score as high as genuine elephant calls, so no threshold cleanly separates them. Fixing this requires retraining with hard-negative mining (see train_binary_detector.py + build_manifest.py), which needs the training dataset (ESC-50 / UrbanSound8K negatives + elephant positives via download.py).
notes: Threshold and pooling here are consumed by both test_elephant_classifier.py and live_elephant_detect.py. To prioritize precision over recall, raise selected_threshold toward 0.5.
